records.name: Mama-Tee Community Fridge Project
records.summary: A network of about 18 community fridges stocked with fresh food, plus a free Saturday pop-up grocery on Washington Avenue. Neighbors can take what they need, and volunteers help keep the fridges full.
records.what_you_do: Take food from a fridge or come to the Saturday pop-up. Volunteers and donors can use the group's volunteer and donate pages.

schedule.text: Free pop-up grocery on Saturdays at 1 pm. Fridges are restocked each week.

first_step.how: Go to the Saturday pop-up or any fridge. To help, use the volunteer page or call the number on the site.
first_step.basis: The pop-up is public and the site lists no eligibility rules

records.notes: The group's fridge address list is on a linked page that was not readable, so only the pop-up address is recorded. The site shows no dated posts. Keep an eye on the Saturday schedule.

records.name: South Philadelphia Community Fridge
records.summary: A volunteer-run set of fridges and pantries across South Philadelphia, stocked with produce, pantry staples and prepared meals that would otherwise go to waste.
records.what_you_do: Take food from any listed fridge, or sign up through the volunteer form to help stock and clean them.

schedule.text: The fridges are open to anyone. The group does not publish set hours.

first_step.how: Use the volunteer sign-up form linked from the site, or email the group with questions
first_step.basis: Volunteer sign-up is public and the fridges are open to anyone

records.notes: The site lists eight fridge addresses but does not match names to addresses. A 2025 guide counts seven. The site footer reads 2025 and posts no dates. A newer Grays Ferry fridge at Universal Audenried High School has no published address.

records.name: Share Food Program
records.summary: A food bank in Hunting Park that runs a community fridge and pantry outside its warehouse, a food rescue program, and a network of partner pantries across the region.
records.what_you_do: Get food from the fridge or a partner pantry, or volunteer to pack food, make calls or help on the farm.

schedule.text: Fridge and pantry hours vary by site. Check the Community Fridges and Find A Food Site pages.

cost.text: Free for people who need food

first_step.how: Call the main line or use the contact form to ask about a fridge, pantry or volunteer shift
first_step.basis: Public phone line and volunteer options are listed, though eligibility rules are not stated

records.notes: The home page carries a feature dated August 2026. Eligibility for the fridge and pantries is not stated on the home page. Philly Food Rescue is recorded as its own entry.

records.name: Philly Food Rescue
records.summary: A volunteer driver program run through Share Food Program. Volunteers pick up surplus food from grocers, restaurants and markets and bring it to pantries, shelters, schools and community fridges.
records.what_you_do: Claim a pickup in the app, collect the food, deliver it to the matched site, and log the rescue. Each run takes about an hour.

schedule.text: Rescues are claimed in the app, one time or on a recurring basis, any time that fits

first_step.how: Download the Philly Food Rescue app, make a profile, turn on notifications and claim a rescue
first_step.basis: Anyone can sign up in the app. Drivers need a license and insurance, and a bike or transit pass works for smaller runs

records.notes: The volunteer page has no dated posts and the group does not publish a driver email. Requirements listed: a license and insurance for driving, a clear space for boxes, lifting 30 lbs, and a phone. Some Wawa runs need coolers that Share supplies.

records.name: The People's Fridge
records.summary: A West Philadelphia food group that runs free pop-up food giveaways and a warehouse that rescues and passes along groceries to community fridges.
records.what_you_do: Get free groceries at a pop-up on the 2nd and 4th Saturdays, or help with food rescue and distribution.

schedule.text: Free pop-ups on the 2nd and 4th Saturdays of the month, 2 to 4 pm

first_step.how: Come to a Saturday pop-up at Cedar Park. Volunteer contact is through the group's Contact page.
first_step.basis: Pop-ups are free and open to neighbors, and the page lists no eligibility rules

records.notes: Per its own site, the group no longer runs a street fridge since moving into a warehouse in 2025. It names several fridges it supplies (Poppi, Pentridge, LAVA, and two Mama-Tee fridges). Volunteering is not described on the page.

records.name: Germantown Community Fridge
records.summary: A mutual aid project that keeps two sidewalk fridges and pantries in Germantown stocked with free food. Volunteers stock, clean and pick up donations.
records.what_you_do: Take food from either fridge, or volunteer to organize, clean, collect donations or shop for groceries.

schedule.text: Fridges are open to anyone. Hours are not listed on the home page.

first_step.how: Email the group or use the Get Involved page to volunteer
first_step.basis: Anyone who needs food is welcome, and volunteers are asked to get in touch

records.notes: The site footer reads 2024 and the site has no dated posts. The guide lists these same fridges.

records.name: Friends Fridge Philly
records.summary: A community fridge on West Clearfield Street where neighbors take what they need and leave what they can. Partner sites help keep it stocked.
records.what_you_do: Take food or leave food at the fridge, or sign up through the form to help keep it going.

schedule.text: Open to anyone. Hours are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Visit the fridge, or sign up through the Google form on the site
first_step.basis: The fridge is open to anyone and volunteers sign up through a public form

records.notes: The site has no dated posts. Its partner sites (church and school) are named without addresses and are not recorded.

records.name: Mt. Airy Community Fridge and Pantry
records.summary: A fridge and pantry under the awning at a site on Stenton Avenue in Mt. Airy. Anyone can take items for free, with no sign-up or income check.
records.what_you_do: Take what you need for your household, or volunteer your time and skills at the pantry. The group also offers nutrition education for classes and groups.

schedule.text: Come by when your schedule allows. No set hours are listed.

first_step.how: Come to the awning on Stenton Avenue. No registration is needed. To volunteer, use the Get Involved page.
first_step.basis: No registration and no income check, and the site lists a clear way to volunteer

records.notes: The site gives no street address beyond the Stenton Avenue awning. The address 6900 Stenton Ave comes from the 2025 guide. The site's one announcement is undated.

records.name: Friends Pantry and Community Fridge
records.summary: A pantry and community fridge on the grounds of Arch Street Meeting House in Old City. Anyone in need can ask for help, and the pantry builds packages for each household.
records.what_you_do: Stop by the community fridge on weekdays, book a Sunday pantry pickup, or call to ask about volunteering or donating.

schedule.text: Community fridge open on weekdays from 8 am until dusk. Pantry pickups by appointment on Sundays, 1 to 2 pm.

first_step.how: Call or text (267) 334-0433 or email to book a pantry pickup or ask about volunteering
first_step.basis: The page says there are no minimum requirements and anyone in need can ask for help

records.notes: The page lists current hours, but its only dated item is a November 2023 ribbon cutting, so the status rule puts it in dormant. Confirm by phone before sending anyone. Status should move to active if the group confirms it is running.

records.name: Ronnie Vega Memorial People's Fridge at LAVA
records.summary: A food pantry on Lancaster Avenue in West Philadelphia, stocked with leftovers and neighbor donations. It also hosts a monthly free market.
records.what_you_do: Take food at the Monday food share or the Thursday food distro, or come to the second Saturday free market.

schedule.text: Mondays 3 to 5 pm food share. Thursdays 3 to 4 pm food distro. Second Saturday 9 am to noon free market.

first_step.how: Come on a posted food share, distro or free market day. The fridge's Instagram is the only direct contact listed.
first_step.basis: Serves neighbors on posted days and lists no eligibility rules

records.notes: The program page has no dated post. Volunteer and donation details are only on LAVA's general donate page.

records.name: The Philadelphia Project
records.summary: A faith-based nonprofit that runs free home repairs for neighbors in Germantown and Mt. Airy, with volunteers joining short service trips that work on those homes.
records.what_you_do: Join a service trip such as a day of service, a blitz weekend or a summer project, or apply for a repair through the Home Repair page.

schedule.text: Service trips run through the year, including a summer of service, blitz weekends, spring break and days of service

cost.text: Repair cost is not stated on the home page

first_step.how: Read the Home Repair page for how a repair works, and use the Get Involved page to pick a service trip
first_step.basis: Service trips are listed publicly on the site, though the sign-up steps are not spelled out

records.notes: The home page has no dated posts, so status is a guess from a working site. Eligibility for repairs is on the Home Repair page, which was not read. The address and phone seen on a listing site were not recorded because that listing is a lead source, not the group's own page. Check the group's Contact page before publishing contact details.

records.name: Rebuilding Together Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that makes free home repairs for homeowners who qualify, with a focus on safety, health and energy. Volunteers join neighborhood block builds where many homes are fixed in two days.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on a block build or as an individual or group, or apply for a repair through the Get Repairs page.

schedule.text: Block builds are two-day volunteer events. The site lists no dated events.

cost.text: Repairs are free for eligible homeowners and tenants

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer page on the site to sign up for a block build, or email info@rebuildingphilly.org
first_step.basis: Volunteering is open to all skill levels, per the site

records.notes: The site footer reads 2022 and it lists block builds and events with no dates. The newest dated item found is an April 2024 news piece, so the status rule puts it in dormant. A listing site gave a different phone number (267-254-5595), which was not used. Check before publishing. Eligibility details were not on the home page.

records.name: Broad Street Love
records.summary: A downtown nonprofit, formerly Broad Street Ministry, that offers meals, mail, a clothing boutique, hygiene items and help with work, benefits, health care and housing, every weekday.
records.what_you_do: Come in on a weekday for a meal, mail, clothing or help finding services. Volunteers sign up for meal, clothing or mail shifts.

schedule.text: Open to guests every weekday. Specific hours are not listed.

first_step.how: Walk in on a weekday, or sign up for a volunteer shift on the volunteer calendar
first_step.basis: Open on weekdays with no eligibility rules listed, and volunteer shifts are posted publicly

records.notes: The site shows only copyright and upload-folder dates. The group's own page does not say who qualifies for services, and it does not use the word homelessness, so the audience is stated as public.

records.name: Prevention Point Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that works with people who are homeless or use drugs. It offers HIV and hepatitis testing and treatment, wound care, a drop-in center, and a mobile health unit.
records.what_you_do: Get testing, treatment or wound care, visit the drop-in center, or volunteer and intern.

schedule.text: Drop-in center and mobile unit. Hours are not listed on the home page.

first_step.how: Visit the drop-in center, or use the Contact Us page for current hours and services
first_step.basis: Services are public, and the home page points to a contact page and a volunteer page

records.notes: This is a health and harm reduction group more than a food or housing group. It is kept here because it offers homeless outreach and drop-in services. The home page has no dated posts and no phone number. Cost of services is not stated.

records.name: Operation Save Our City
records.summary: A Kensington group with a space called Sunshine House, offering outreach, a food drive, neighborhood clean-ups and help for people facing addiction and homelessness.
records.what_you_do: Help with a food drive or clean-up, or get involved through the group's Get Involved page.

schedule.text: Days and hours are not listed on the home page

cost.text: Donations accepted; cost of services not stated

records.notes: The home page names services but gives no days, hours, address, volunteer steps or contact details. The Contact, Get Involved and About pages were linked but not read. Verify before publishing those details. No dated posts were visible.

records.name: Philly Unknown Project
records.summary: A grassroots group in Kensington that does street outreach, packs harm-reduction care bags, and runs the Ruth Street Garden with a mural project and community learning.
records.what_you_do: Help with outreach, pack care bags, support events or the hub, pick up donations, or help with the garden.

schedule.text: No days or hours are listed. Volunteers arrange shifts by email.

first_step.how: Email PhillyUnknownProject@gmail.com or use the contact form on the site
first_step.basis: The site names a clear email for joining, and volunteer roles are listed

records.notes: The home page has no dated posts. The January 2025 article lists food drives and transitional housing, but the home page does not mention either, so neither is claimed here.

records.name: Unity Clinic
records.summary: A free clinic on South 21st Street in South Philadelphia for uninsured patients. Volunteer nurses, doctors and students staff it on Tuesday evenings.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as a nurse, clinician or student on a Tuesday evening shift.

schedule.text: Tuesdays, 5 to 8 pm. Volunteers arrive from 4:30 pm.

first_step.how: Nurse practitioners and physicians contact the clinic's volunteer coordinator. Nursing and medical students go through their school programs.
first_step.basis: Clinicians need a license and a set volunteer commitment, and students join through their schools

records.notes: The source is a Villanova partner page, not the clinic's own site, and it has no publish date. The 2006 founding is the only date. Verify the Tuesday schedule before sending anyone. Volunteer contacts are individual staff and were not recorded. Interpreting services in Spanish and Bahasa Indonesia are listed on the page.

records.name: Greater Philadelphia Community Alliance (housing counseling)
records.summary: Counselors who help renters and homeowners who are behind on payments, with budget help, eviction prevention through payment assistance when funds are available, and landlord and tenant mediation.
records.what_you_do: Book an appointment to talk through money problems, eviction, foreclosure, or buying a first home.

schedule.text: Appointments only, Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm

cost.text: Counseling is free. A $25 fee applies if a credit report is needed.

first_step.how: Call (215) 336-5505 or apply through the online intake form to set up an appointment
first_step.basis: Anyone behind on payments or at risk of losing a home can book an appointment by phone or online

records.notes: Source is a PA211 directory listing, which has no update date. No website is listed. Eviction payment help depends on available funds, so ask before counting on it.

records.name: New Kensington Community Development Corporation (housing counseling)
records.summary: A free housing counseling office for residents of ZIP code 19134. Counselors help with rent, utilities, mortgages, foreclosure, property tax and rent rebates, and budgeting.
records.what_you_do: Call or email for an intake appointment with a HUD-certified housing counselor.

schedule.text: Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm

first_step.basis: Limited to ZIP 19134 residents, and intake is by phone or email

records.notes: Source is a PA211 directory listing with no website or email and no update date. The listing says the office helps with affordable home repair referrals, which was not checked.

leads_only.note: Fetched, but the site does not name a city or service area, so it is not recorded as Philadelphia. The January 2025 Inquirer roundup lists it under mutual aid. Confirm the city first.

leads_only.note: Free clothing and household goods pop-ups, including Free Library branches. The library event page returned HTTP 403, and the group's own site was not identified. Find its own site before recording.

leads_only.name: The Wardrobe
leads_only.note: Philadelphia clothing nonprofit with a 4th and Callow Hill location, named in search results only. Not fetched.

leads_only.name: Pentridge Fridge
leads_only.note: Named on The People's Fridge site at 5110 Pentridge St. No own site found.

leads_only.name: Umoja Community Fridge
leads_only.note: At 2206 W Jefferson Ave in the 2025 guide. Only an Instagram link is known.

leads_only.note: Pop-up free medical, dental and vision events in Philadelphia, most recently August 2025, per a WHYY/Inquirer search summary. Group's own site not fetched.

leads_only.name: University City Hospitality Coalition clinic (Penn medical students)
leads_only.note: Free clinic at St. Agatha-St. James church, 38th and Chestnut, serving homeless residents on Wednesday nights, per a Penn Medicine document that is itself dated. Not fetched.

leads_only.note: Fetched. A national food rescue group whose page does not mention Philadelphia, so it was dropped as not local. Philly-area volunteer driver listing on PA211 is unverified.

leads_only.note: Idealist volunteer listing in June and July 2026. Not checked; leads platform only and no group site found.

leads_only.note: Same group as the Mama-Tee record. Not separately recorded.

notes: Verdict counts: publish 19, hide 0, not_a_group 0, duplicate 0, out_of_area 0. Searches used: 9 of 10. Fetches: about 46. Two sites returned 404 (Double Trellis) and one did not resolve (Coral Street Fridge). Three records are low confidence because their sites are undated or only dated by footer: Rebuilding Together (site dated 2022, status dormant), Friends Pantry at Arch Street (dormant by the dated-evidence rule, although hours are listed), and Unity Clinic (source is a Villanova partner page). Sharing Excess was dropped because it does not operate in Philadelphia per its own page. Phone and address facts that came only from listing sites (PA211, Idealist, Benevity) were left out of records where the group's own page did not confirm them, except the PA211-only housing counseling records, which have no own site. Budget ran close to the limit on housing and basic needs searches, so searches for goods closets and free clinics were thin: list pages returned mostly older articles.
